principle: The systems-layer map: the owner's read is that we are building a SYSTEMS LAYER for executable capability (index it = Teleon; govern its truth = Baltor; structure the open knowledge = Open*Hubs; watch usage = Observer), not point products. This file reconciles the owner's proposed 'missing layers' (2026-06-24 strategy feedback) against what ALREADY EXISTS in the repo, names the REAL gap in each, and ranks them under the Foundational Law. COMPUTED-checked: scripts/check_substrate_layers.py asserts every listed asset path exists, so the map cannot silently drift from the code. Most layers already exist (partial→live) — applying the owner's own Layer-8 law to our own architecture: do not rebuild what exists; close the gap.

foundational_law.system_filter: Does this improve COMPILER INTELLIGENCE? If no, do not build it. (Governs what WE build.)
foundational_law.execution_filter: Can intelligence be REMOVED from this execution path? Descend toward that forever. (The Teleon descent thesis: make-it-work -> make-it-cheap -> deterministic substitution.)
foundational_law.component_admission: Two-axis: a component must LIFT over the bare model AND the lift must be STRUCTURAL/durable (won't close when the next model ships). Source: docs/concepts/capability-valleys.md + scripts/eval/reason_codes.py. (Governs what enters the REGISTRIES.)
foundational_law.binding_constraint: DEPTH BEFORE BREADTH. Every new layer must serve the ONE vertical being proven to a paying customer (win-one-vertical), gated by scripts/proposal_backlog.py. Breadth without a proven revenue vertical is the failure mode the owner flagged ('too broad') — and 7 of 8 proposed layers already exist, so the move is reconcile+close-gap, not build-new.
foundational_law.reconciliation: system_filter selects what WE build; component_admission selects what enters the registries; execution_filter is the descent; binding_constraint subordinates all of it to depth/revenue. The owner's law is NECESSARY; the pre-existing laws make it SUFFICIENT.

layers.real_gap: The 7-primitive model + a code-genome index of OUR code exist. Missing: the finer ~25 atomic ops (search/retry/authenticate/parse/extract/validate/transform/dedupe/chunk/classify/cache/normalize/compress/merge/map/join/sort/route) as a first-class registry, AND per-software decomposition (Stripe SDK -> [authenticate, retry, serialize, validate, http, parse, rate-limit]).
layers.law_justification: Atomic decomposition lets the compiler reason about software at primitive level -> improves compiler intelligence.

layers.real_gap: Providers + pricebook + topology + (cold_start, gpu in capability_runtime_classes) exist. Missing: unified per-provider deployment-economics metadata across Modal/RunPod/Replicate/Railway/Fly/AWS/Cloudflare/GCP/Azure — egress cost, concurrency limits, region availability, cold-start-ms — so the compiler can price deployment, not just inference.
layers.law_justification: The compiler should know deployment economics to choose where to run -> improves compiler intelligence. HIGH-ROI, concrete.

layers.real_gap: GitHub + tool harvesting + repo-similarity + a registry dependency graph exist. Missing: cross-ecosystem ingestion (PyPI/npm/DockerHub/HuggingFace) with co-installation / co-occurrence statistics ('75% of OCR repos also use pdfplumber') at scale.
layers.law_justification: Machine intelligence about software ecosystems -> the compiler can recommend the proven stack and detect reinvention -> improves compiler intelligence.

layers.real_gap: AI-usage intervention heuristics + session capture exist. Missing: MINED human-workflow patterns from captured sessions ('this manual workflow repeated 240x -> automation opportunity') aggregated into a registry. Capture exists; the mining/aggregation does not.
layers.law_justification: Detecting repeated human workflows feeds the automation/descent pipeline -> improves compiler intelligence.

layers.real_gap: This IS AIDevObserver + economics + inefficient-pipeline archetypes — waste detection (oversized PDF to frontier, duplicate context, overprompting, frontier-when-small-suffices, browser-when-API-exists) is live. Amplification (valid): crystallize the patterns into a first-class queryable AI Waste Registry with a {pattern, avoidable_cost, avoidable_tokens} schema, and grow Observer into a standalone product.
layers.law_justification: Directly the execution_filter ('remove unnecessary intelligence') -> core compiler intelligence.

layers.real_gap: adapter_factory.from_openapi(spec) already turns a whole OpenAPI spec into one typed component per endpoint (N×M -> N+M). Missing: factories for Docker-container -> component and arbitrary-Python-package -> capability-graph-node.
layers.law_justification: Auto-converting ecosystems into components grows the registry without manual onboarding -> improves compiler intelligence.

layers.real_gap: The PREDICTIVE substrate exists: durability_class + decay_signal (reason_codes.py), the durable-gap harness, and an inference-time capability watch doc. The 'futures MARKET' itself is DEFERRED BY DESIGN (repo strategy + owner-internalized 'win one vertical first' / don't-build-discovery-at-scale-or-capability-futures-yet). Honest pushback: a predictive market is speculative and hard to validate before one vertical earns revenue.
layers.law_justification: Two-axis admission already IS a capability-futures judgment (is the lift durable?). Elevate the watch, defer the market until a vertical is proven.

layers.proposed_name: Existing Systems Registry (Registry 100 — 'this already exists, do not build it')
layers.real_gap: The reinvention guard + the registry federation + tool harvesting + a no-reinvention rubric implement the 'already exists' decision engine for tools/repos/components. Missing: a comprehensive existing-systems corpus (complete SaaS products / enterprise software / internal codebases) feeding it. The DECISION ENGINE exists; the CORPUS breadth is the gap.
layers.law_justification: The owner calls this potentially 'the highest ROI decision engine.' It exists in core (reinvention_guard) — feed it, don't rebuild it.
